content: Hmm. Two downstream repos which I'm maintaining are finding it hard to adapt to this linter (which just got turned on in mathlib), because there is a hard-coded "it's OK if the declaration ends in _mathlib" exception (see here ) which does not apply to declarations ending in e.g. _fLT (of which I have several in FLT, all autogenerated of course). Just remarking this -- I can have them in nolints.json (but I was rather proud to have an empty nolints.json file up until this point ;-) )

Fair! Sadly, there's no way to enable an environment linter on all of mathlib while disabling it downstream --- and there's also no easy way to create a syntax linter while annotating several hundreds of exceptions. I hope the upcoming FRO work on linters will fix this.
Surely you can figure out in which module the definition is defined (e.g. Mathlib or FLT), and then see if the name ends in an underscore plus that.
Presumably we can reuse the functions that Lean is using to generate these suffixed names?

docs#Lean.Elab.Command.mkInstanceName which calls docs#Lean.Elab.Command.NameGen.mkBaseNameWithSuffix
So maybe

private def moduleToSuffix : Name → String
  | .anonymous => ""
  | .num n _ => moduleToSuffix n
  | .str n s => moduleToSuffix n ++ "_" ++ s.decapitalize

def endsWithProjectSuffix (name : Name) : MetaM Bool := do
  let moduleName ← getMainModule
  let project := moduleName.getRoot
  return name.toString.endsWith <| moduleToSuffix project

Or moduleName := env.allImportedModuleNames[env.getModuleIdxFor? name |>.getD default]! if env linters can run with a different main module than the one they're linting
Bit of a tangent, but does anyone know why Mathlib.Tactic definitions are allowed to have underscores?
(Btw, I'm taking a quick look at this linter.)

Thomas Murrills said:

Bit of a tangent, but does anyone know why Mathlib.Tactic definitions are allowed to have underscores?

I think the idea is that these definitions are very likely to be internal to a tactic, and while this means they need to be public, they aren't meant to be user-facing, and thus are acceptable exceptions to this naming convention linter
(this list doesn't line up exactly, but has substantial overlap: https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=%22Mathlib.Tactic.%22%2C%22_%22 and I don't think some of these are worth changing)

Bhavik Mehta said:

I think the idea is that these definitions are very likely to be internal to a tactic, and while this means they need to be public, they aren't meant to be user-facing, and thus are acceptable exceptions to this naming convention linter

True, but they're still user-facing if you're a metaprogramming user! :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes: My point being that I think it still makes sense to lint them to keep our meta code nice and readable. As such I agree the names of "helper mathematical objects" don't matter so much, but I'd say the names of meta code defs still do, and we should just nolint the ones that don't matter.
Experimenting with some alternative choices in #39890.
(A lot of _ names in that list are ParserDescrs and can be removed on that basis instead, for instance. Presumably this is what downstream projects need too.)
Can this linter be disabled for macros/tactics? There's already a precedent underscores are fine for those, see e.g. ac_refl.

Those fall under ParserDescrs - they're currently disabled in the linter because of Mathlib.Tactic but my understanding is that Thomas wants to disable them because they have type ParserDescr? (In either case, I think everyone's agreed that these should be allowed to have underscores!)

Violeta Hernández said:

Can this linter be disabled for macros/tactics? There's already a precedent underscores are fine for those, see e.g. ac_refl.

actually docs#Lean.Parser.Tactic.acRfl doesn't have any underscores in it, a better example would be an autogenerated name like docs#Nat.term_!

Well, I'm currently getting lint errors in things such as

macro "of_sets_tactic" : tactic => ...

Yeah, in my proposed changes the ParserDescr (or TrailingParserDescr) creating that error would indeed be exempt for the reason Bhavik said :)

(Note: the other definition of type Macro created by that command is in turn created by aux_def and has a component beginning with _, and therefore is exempt by an (already-present) isAutoDecl, no changes needed from me.)

One thing I'm a bit iffy about is instances. Currently I'm proposing "if the decl is an instance, ignore components starting with inst". But this allows things like instance instFoo_bar, which do occur in mathlib. Still, if a name ends in _, like Foo_, and we have an autogenerated instFoo_Bar, that's fine.

I'd like to regenerate the instance name and compare, but it's somewhat awkward, and I'm not confident about which binders it's using (or if I could just use the type).

Does anyone have any suggestions or opinions?
#mathlib4 > Underscore in Mat_ btw
Aha, interesting. Aside, but I'm guessing docs#ModuleCat.MonModuleEquivalenceAlgebra.Algebra_of_Mon_ is now—or was always, given the extra underscores around of—misnamed? :eyes:

Thomas Murrills said:

Does anyone have any suggestions or opinions?

If we transition to a syntax linter we could just check that the instance doesn't have a name and then ignore it, right?
Otherwise, I think regenerating the name is best.
Makes sense. Though, should we consider terminal _ tech debt? :eyes: In that case we don't need to exempt any instance names beyond exempting _<number> and _<project> I think, right?

I'm wondering more generally now about names like docs#CategoryTheory.section_ and docs#CategoryTheory.Limits.end_ . Why are these named the way they are? Should this sort of definition naming be documented in the style guide, or should they be renamed? (I feel we should definitely do one or the other. :) )

Aren't some of those namespaced under a (correctly-named) theorem, e.g. docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.OneHypercoverDenseData.isSheaf_iff.fac under docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.OneHypercoverDenseData.isSheaf_iff ? Do we definitely want to ban that? I think it's okay if the namespace refers to an actual theorem.
I think it's pretty strange, namespaces are usually about dot-notation. If something is namespaced under a theorem I'd expect it to be an auxiliary theorem, and thus private.

Hmm, I'm not sure I agree that organized-as-auxiliary ↔︎ private necesssarily (and I think namespaces are just as good for organization as for dot notation)...but yeah, these do seem to be auxiliary theorems and defs.

Thomas Murrills said:

I'm wondering more generally now about names like docs#CategoryTheory.section_ and docs#CategoryTheory.Limits.end_ . Why are these named the way they are?

We can't call them CategoryTheory.section or CategoryTheory.end because section and end are reserved keywords.

Thomas Murrills said:

Aren't some of those namespaced under a (correctly-named) theorem, e.g. docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.OneHypercoverDenseData.isSheaf_iff.fac under docs#CategoryTheory.Functor.OneHypercoverDenseData.isSheaf_iff ? Do we definitely want to ban that? I think it's okay if the namespace refers to an actual theorem.

I think the names are perfectly fine: The namespace here is used to organize a family of auxiliary declarations to prove isSheaf_iff. However, #39959 makes them private.

Christian Merten said:

We can't call them CategoryTheory.section or CategoryTheory.end because section and end are reserved keywords.

In that case keyword + "_" sounds like a fine exception to have.
Though it's pretty strange that endofunctor ≠ end of a functor
Or maybe we could use end' instead?
How about «end» --- does that work?
We could also do something funny with syntax (declaring "section" as term syntax, and trying to get it not to conflict in various ways) if we really wanted to. (But that might be nontrivial.)

Michael Rothgang said:

How about «end» --- does that work?

I know there are examples of this but I think we should prefer things that are easier to type like end_ or end'
note that we do something similar with docs#Lean.Expr.letE and docs#Lean.Expr.forallE
I suppose that would suggest endC or maybe even catEnd...
(Note: to go back one topic in this thread, I've asked about the conventionality of theorems-as-namespaces more broadly in #mathlib4 > Naming convention, here)

Put weak.linter.defsWithUnderscore = false (unsure about the name of the linter) in your lakefile.toml

From the error messages, that name is right.

weak.linter.defsWithUnderscore = false
I do not know if the order matters, but the order you have now agrees with what I do myself (with the header linter)
I tried reversing the order and it did not change anything. I'll lake update and see what happens.
lake update is irrelevant here. Did you however restart the Lean server?
Yes, I restarted (by restarting VSCode). I still get the errors both with #lint in VSCode and with lake exe runLinter LeanMachineLearning on the command line. Strange.
I'm working on the branch of https://github.com/LeanMachineLearning/LML/pull/114 by the way.
That linter is an environment linter. Sadly, I don't know how to disable that downstream.
The lakefile options are for syntax linters (i.e., the ones giving you yellow squiggles, which you enable or disable with set_option linter.foo.bar false in)
So, if it cannot be turned off, how do I know what thing I need to write in nolints.json to ignore the errors?
I opened Mathlib's nolints.json and found the answer there.
By the way, you should be able to create a nolints.json that records all the current violations as nolints via lake exe runLinter --update
(Also, I’ll mention that these two linting frameworks will be given a much nicer, more unified UX by the FRO in the not-too-distant future and hopefully lake exe runLinter will become obsolete :) )

In FLT this triggered a huge number of false positives ending in _fLT and I just added them to nolints.json with the command above. This was annoying because my nolints.json used to be empty but now there are things there which I cannot remove (until someone changes the linter so that instead of saying "ignore names that end in _mathlib" it says "ignore names that end in the name of the project")
#39890 should fix this
It is possible that lean4#13893 (just merged into core) will also help addressing this issue.
